investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T22:07–22:14Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~145–148 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 and producing any evidence. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is also blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have a fixed kata.peerpods.io/vm limit, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their VM resources, the resource counter may be artificially depleted. The withCleanup wrapper at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 is intended to handle cleanup, but a prior failed or interrupted run may have left resources allocated.

Lower confidence — cluster-level quota or limit range change reducing the total kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quantity on the 2 matching nodes: no source or incident evidence supports this, but it cannot be ruled out without inspecting node capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available on the 2 affinity-matching nodes with no pods consuming it, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug or misconfiguration.

If the remote-agent-create eval passed on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure would be transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only one of the three sibling checks failed while the others passed, a shared infrastructure exhaustion would be less likely and the cause would be localized to that specific check's pod spec or timing.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to have correct labels matching the pod's affinity/selector after a node label audit, the affinity constraint would not be a contributing factor and the root cause would be solely the 2-node VM slot limit.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node (i.e., the resource was removed or renamed), the failure mode would be a missing resource definition rather than exhaustion.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/nodeAffinity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting early if node label drift reduces the schedulable pool.

Add a zombie-VM detection eval that lists pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and flags any that have been in a non-Running state for longer than the expected agent lifecycle, to catch cleanup failures from the withCleanup wrapper.

Consider adding a latency-band eval that warns when remote-agent pod scheduling exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) before the full 148s unschedulable timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T22:09–22:14Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is left in Unschedulable state. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers pod scheduling; that scheduling fails before any agent identity or state can be captured, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to remain absent and the check to time out at ~148 s. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): contract requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none present because the pod never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and the remaining 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims exist, so capacity cannot be reclaimed automatically.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to vm-resource exhaustion.
Tertiary — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, leaving none for the probe pods.

Lower probability — a recent cluster scaling event or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb probe traffic alongside production workloads.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 22:09 and 22:14 UTC on 2026-06-29 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime response contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was never satisfied.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable for ~145–148 seconds before the eval times out, and no agent runtime response is ever produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available VM slots and they have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool under-provisioned: only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, and the pool size is insufficient to absorb simultaneous eval probe submissions (all three sibling checks submitted pods within a ~5-minute window).

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not complete successfully in a prior run, orphaned pods may be occupying the resource.

Quaternary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration narrowing the eligible pool: the 4 non-kata nodes may have been recently reconfigured or labeled in a way that excludes them from remote agent scheduling, effectively shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T22:07–22:14Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~145–148 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 and producing any evidence. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is also blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have a fixed kata.peerpods.io/vm limit, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their VM resources, the resource counter may be artificially depleted. The withCleanup wrapper at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 is intended to handle cleanup, but a prior failed or interrupted run may have left resources allocated.

Lower confidence — cluster-level quota or limit range change reducing the total kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quantity on the 2 matching nodes: no source or incident evidence supports this, but it cannot be ruled out without inspecting node capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 22:09 and 22:14 UTC on 2026-06-29 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime response contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was never satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable for ~145–148 seconds before the eval times out, and no agent runtime response is ever produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=152942 endedAt=2026-06-29T22:14:37.783Z — eval ran to near-timeout before failing.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the agent pod never reached a running state, so no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was captured.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe never receiving a runtime response.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable scheduler message, latencyMs=152803, endedAt=2026-06-29T22:09:36.467Z — the create step failed first with the same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable scheduler message, latencyMs=148374, endedAt=2026-06-29T22:12:04.841Z — the state step also failed before runtime was attempted.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which submits the pod that the scheduler cannot place.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=152942 is well under the outage threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduler rejection, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available VM slots and they have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool under-provisioned: only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, and the pool size is insufficient to absorb simultaneous eval probe submissions (all three sibling checks submitted pods within a ~5-minute window).

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not complete successfully in a prior run, orphaned pods may be occupying the resource.

Quaternary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration narrowing the eligible pool: the 4 non-kata nodes may have been recently reconfigured or labeled in a way that excludes them from remote agent scheduling, effectively shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Observe whether the pod is again stuck Unschedulable with the kata.peerpods.io/vm message.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling bottleneck
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool is the shared constraint.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and allocations in the production cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe nodes) to check the Allocatable and Allocated quantities for kata.peerpods.io/vm on each node, and list any pods currently holding that resource.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for orphaned or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: List pods in the remote-agent namespace or with the relevant labels to identify any that were not cleaned up by withCleanup and are still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent VM scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes, directly blocking pod placement for all remote agent eval checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduler error within a 5-minute window, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked by the capacity constraint.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner remote agent creation path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 1913–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that cannot be scheduled. No evidence is collected because the pod never starts.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all five are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence) because the agent pod never reached a running state.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production Kubernetes cluster immediately to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs. Allocated counts on the 2 eligible nodes and identify what is consuming the capacity.

Check for orphaned remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs; terminate any stuck pods to free VM slots.
Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool (currently 2 of 6 nodes) is sized appropriately for concurrent eval probe submissions plus any production workloads sharing the same resource.

Investigate why 4 of 6 nodes do not match the remote agent pod's node affinity or selector — confirm this is intentional configuration and not a recent labeling change that inadvertently reduced the eligible pool.

Consider staggering the three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) in the scheduled workflow to reduce simultaneous VM slot demand, or add a pre-check that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before submitting pods.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 185); confirm the feature's degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold (line 187) is being evaluated correctly given all three sibling checks are currently failing.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still present or was transient. A pass would indicate the capacity was freed; a repeat Unschedulable failure confirms sustained exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and current allocations
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the resource exhaustion hypothesis and identifies whether orphaned pods are occupying slots.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run cluster node inspection tooling to check Allocatable vs. Allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm on all 6 nodes and identify which pods are holding the resource.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources in the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out or confirms the leaked-pod hypothesis as a contributing cause.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the cluster for all pods requesting or holding kata.peerpods.io/vm to identify any orphaned eval pods that withCleanup may have missed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state in isolation after capacity check
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling bottleneck affects all remote-agent checks equally, validating that the root cause is at the VM scheduling layer rather than a check-specific issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run a local-agent eval check to confirm non-remote agent paths are healthy
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: A passing local-agent check would confirm the failure is scoped to the kata.peerpods.io/vm remote VM layer and not a broader platform or auth regression.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (non-zero free slots) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime eval immediately after the failure, with no intervening cluster changes, would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes were previously eligible for remote agent pods (i.e., their affinity/selector configuration changed recently) would shift the primary cause to a node pool misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
Presence of no orphaned remote agent pods in the cluster at the time of failure would rule out the leaked-pod hypothesis.

A passing run of local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote VM scheduling layer and not a broader API or auth outage.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote agent creation, reporting available slot count as evidence — this would catch exhaustion before a pod submission timeout.
Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval or post-run assertion that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods remain after each eval cycle, catching withCleanup failures early.

Add a remote-agent-node-pool eval that asserts the number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm meets a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2 with free capacity), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Consider a remote-agent-scheduling-latency eval that measures pod-to-running time and warns if it exceeds a threshold, providing earlier signal before the full eval timeout is reached.
